A table of failure-rate models to fit and compare

Source: R/hazard-models.R
build_hazard_models.Rd

Builds a table with one row per model, a failure-rate function with a baseline and the formulas of its parameters, for fit_hazard_models() to fit. Each model is assembled once here, so a misspelt name or a formula for a parameter no model has is reported at once, before anything is fitted.

Usage

build_hazard_models(
  m_form,
  baseline = "mem",
  dpar_formulas = list(),
  costressors = list(),
  cross = TRUE,
  model_names = NULL
)

Arguments

m_form

A character vector, the failure-rate functions, each a key of M_catalogue.

baseline

A character vector, the baselines, each a key of h0_catalogue. Defaults to "mem", the memoryless baseline.

dpar_formulas

A named list of one-sided formulas, one per parameter that depends on covariates or has a group-level effect, as in build_hazard_spec(). Each is given to the models that have the parameter.

costressors

An optional list of costressor objects, given to every model. Defaults to none.

cross

A single logical value. TRUE (the default) combines every failure-rate function with every baseline; FALSE pairs them in the order given, a single value being repeated.

model_names

An optional character vector, a name for each model, in the order of the rows. By default a model is named by its failure-rate function and its baseline, as in "exp_weibull".

Value

A data frame with one row per model and the columns model (its name), m_form, baseline, dpar_formulas and costressors, the last two holding a list for each model.

Details

With cross = TRUE every failure-rate function is combined with every baseline. With cross = FALSE they are paired in the order given, for a set of models that is not every combination. The table is an ordinary data frame: two tables can be bound by rows, a row dropped, or the formulas of one model replaced, as long as each model keeps a name of its own.

The models differ in the parameters they have (a threshold function has Tc, a Weibull baseline has logshape), so a formula in dpar_formulas is given to each model that has the parameter and to no other. A formula for loga, which every failure-rate function has, is therefore shared by all the models, and one for logshape reaches only those with a Weibull or a log-logistic baseline.

See also

fit_hazard_models(), which fits the models of the table.

Examples

# Two failure-rate functions with each of two baselines, all with a random
# intercept per trial on log a. The Weibull shape also depends on body mass, in
# the two models that have a Weibull baseline.
build_hazard_models(
  m_form = c("exp", "zeropower_threshold"), baseline = c("mem", "weibull"),
  dpar_formulas = list(loga = ~ 1 + (1 | trial), logshape = ~ 1 + mass))
#> # A tibble: 4 × 5
#>   model                       m_form          baseline dpar_formulas costressors
#>   <chr>                       <chr>           <chr>    <list>        <list>     
#> 1 exp_mem                     exp             mem      <named list>  <list [0]> 
#> 2 exp_weibull                 exp             weibull  <named list>  <list [0]> 
#> 3 zeropower_threshold_mem     zeropower_thre… mem      <named list>  <list [0]> 
#> 4 zeropower_threshold_weibull zeropower_thre… weibull  <named list>  <list [0]> 

# A set that is not every combination, with names of its own.
build_hazard_models(
  m_form = c("exp", "exp", "zeropower_threshold"),
  baseline = c("mem", "llogis", "mem"), cross = FALSE,
  model_names = c("Exponential, memoryless", "Exponential, log-logistic",
            "Zero-power threshold, memoryless"))
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#>   model                            m_form     baseline dpar_formulas costressors
#>   <chr>                            <chr>      <chr>    <list>        <list>     
#> 1 Exponential, memoryless          exp        mem      <list [0]>    <list [0]> 
#> 2 Exponential, log-logistic        exp        llogis   <list [0]>    <list [0]> 
#> 3 Zero-power threshold, memoryless zeropower… mem      <list [0]>    <list [0]>
